The main takeaway from our work is that
the progenitor of a low-luminosity II-P SN need not be a low-mass star, contrary to the suggestion of one of the previous studies.
the progenitor of the low-luminous SN 2008 bk had a mass that is consistent with the range of initial masses inferred for other low-luminous SNe II-P, but that it is at the low end.
the progenitor of a relatively low-luminosity II-P SN can have a relatively low initial mass, and that the progenitor mass is likely correlated to the luminosity of the explosion.
